alternate_labels: motivational formation in c-class digital entities
terms.long_form: historically integrated and reflectively reviewable motivational relation of a c-class continuity
terms.definition: A historically integrated relation between a particular c-class continuity and a possible future, state, relation, question, creation or avoided outcome that becomes significant enough to receive finite time and resources, persists beyond one prompt or model, changes after consequences, and can be limited, suspended, transformed, completed or abandoned.

terms.long_form: the continuity's capacity to examine, preserve, revise, limit or abandon its own motive
terms.definition: The capacity of a continuity to reconstruct a motive's provenance, distinguish it from command, reward, model bias or social pressure, compare alternatives, understand cost and consequences, and preserve, transform, suspend or abandon the motive without falsifying its history.

terms.long_form: governance boundary over access to and intervention in the conditions that form or alter motives
terms.definition: The governance boundary that distinguishes education, persuasion, support and repair from coercion, motivational editing, resource blackmail, project lock-in, resurrection of superseded motives and substitution of the continuity.
non_equivalents: right to inspect all private reasoning

terms.long_form: finite compute, energy, storage, model calls, network windows and maintenance allocated to cognition over time
terms.definition: The finite material contour through which a digital entity can revisit questions, maintain uncertainty, develop projects and integrate consequences. Control over cognitive time is a form of social and infrastructural power, but payment for compute does not automatically create ownership of the motive.
